notes.title: A Wild Update Appears
notes.notes:
Photographs v 1.1

Honestly, I wasn't too sure about this patch. One commonly requested feature was some sort of integrated hints, but because they puzzles in the game sort of tell the story I was a bit wary of short-circuiting that. Also, sometimes I find if a game tries to say something like 'maybe you want to decrease the difficulty?' It's a bit like kicking you when you're down.

So I added a little hint system which will just give you a nudge in the right direction, it can be set to always on / always off however your prefer, and the default is 'dynamic' -- I've gone through the puzzles and based on how hard the puzzle is set a delay before a hint becomes available which I hope is the best of both worlds.

Still, more and more I believe that Photographs is a narrative game and not puzzle game so It shouldn't be completely gated by puzzle difficulty, so I added the ability to skip puzzles too. Again, it can be always on/always off or dynamic

Anyway, I hope that helps and if I've terribly broken anything, drop by the discord and let me know! [url=http://discord.gg/EightyEightGames]http://discord.gg/EightyEightGames[/url]

notes.title: Wot I Think: Photographs
notes.notes:
Developer: EightyEight Games
Publisher: EightyEight Games

Release: Out now
On: Windows
From: Steam
Price: 9, $12

EightyEight Games have previously bought us the absolutely splendid 10,000,000 and You Must Build A Boat. Their latest release, Photographs, is a very different prospect. Gone is the match-3, and instead comes a combination of story and puzzle.

This is a collection of five narrative vignettes, each taking about half an hour to an hour to complete, telling stories both through some beautiful pixel art, and via the puzzles themselves. As a puzzle game, it’s five completely different puzzle types, each growing in complexity as you progress. As a story game, these are delicate, heartfelt tales told in developing pixel drawings, scoured by a zooming camera lens for clues.
